target_customer: Organizations running their own GPU and HPC clusters on SLURM or Kubernetes
problem: Teams guess GPU resources before jobs run, so jobs fail or hardware sits reserved and idle.
business_model: Per cluster software pricing with paid pilots, as stated in the launch post coverage
product_category: AI infrastructure software for GPU resource prediction

investors: Angel investors including former DeepMind researchers

competitors.name: NVIDIA Run:ai
competitors.what: GPU orchestration and scheduling for clusters

competitors.name: SLURM and Kubernetes native schedulers
competitors.what: Default scheduling with user supplied resource requests

technical_complexity.rationale: Predicting memory, runtime and failure for arbitrary jobs needs models trained on cluster telemetry; founders built similar predictors at EPCC.

defensibility.rationale: Trained on cluster job data and installed on every node with scheduler hooks, which raises switching costs; models could be copied by scheduler vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found as of November 2026.

market_need_then: The company cites teams reserving 2 to 2.5 times what they use and about $8M of monthly compute waste found at one supercomputing center (company claims).

identity.logo: Icon with orange stroke accents (brand color #F16523 per Brandfetch)
identity.visual_style: Black, white and grey with an orange accent

brand_strength.rationale: Clean identity but a common word shared with a crypto project and other firms; little brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Expanse is a Spring 2026 London YC company whose four founders ran GPU clusters at quant funds and built resource predictors at EPCC. It announced a $5.3M seed in September 2026 led by Crane Venture Partners, early evidence of strong founder market fit. It remains early with paid pilots and company reported benchmarks.
notes: Seed reported by several outlets (xyz.pl, Dealroom news, citybiz, Vestbee); the citybiz page returned 403 so details come from search snippets. FundedIQ lists $5.8M across two rounds, which conflicts and is not recorded. Competitor list uses 2026 sources, no dated competitor search hit beyond launch coverage.
